newsitem.title: NIGERIA: Nigeria says concerned at "hostile" Britain.
newsitem.headline: Nigeria says concerned at "hostile" Britain.

text.p: Nigeria's military rulers on Friday said they were concerned about "hostile and definitely unhelpful" statements made by former colonial power Britain's foreign minister Robin Cook.

A statement from the foreign ministry in the capital Abuja said remarks made by Cook, that the Commonwealth should not lift Nigeria's suspension, were part of a campaign against Nigeria's membership of the club of Britain and its former colonies.
"This is not only malicious but prejudicial to our good standing in the international community," said the statement, issued in the name of military ruler General Sani Abacha.

"It is of great concern to us and other observers of the new Labour government that the British foreign secretary has been making statements about Nigeria which are hostile and definitely unhelpful to the improvement of relations."

Relations between Western countries and Nigeria have been cool since the suspension of the populous, West African state from the Commonwealth in 1995 after the hanging of author Ken Saro-Wiwa and eight other activists.

But Britain's Labour government, elected in May, has promised a tougher line than the previous Conservatives, and last month Cook launched a stinging attack on Nigeria for lack of democracy, human rights abuses and corruption.
The statement said Nigeria believed Cook intended to influence meetings of Commonwealth ministers on the country's suspension, scheduled for July 10 and 11 in London.
"The hostile disposition of the new Labour government ... is at variance with the friendly relations which the Nigerian government is determined to foster with Great Britain," it said.

The statement questioned the relevance of the Commonwealth for Nigerians and repeated an earlier warning that Britain "should not pursue a course of action that could result in the disintegration of the Commonwealth."
Nigeria, a major oil-producer, is one of Britain's biggest trading partners in Africa.
